sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; one generic sentence ('KSL uses hand shapes, movements, spatial grammar, and nonmanual signals', sec. 2.3); cites Al-Dookhi & Alotaibi 2025 and Al-Fityani & Padden as its only KSL-linguistic sources.

sources.citation: Al-Dookhi, Bader & Haya Alotaibi. 2025. Kuwaiti Sign Language. Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Social Sciences Study 6(1): 13-20. doi:10.47616/jamrsss.v6i1.578 (English translation of a chapter of Al-Dookhi 2018, Arabic)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or prosodic prominence. Only sub-lexical structure given: four parameters (handshape, location, movement, orientation), Battison's symmetry and dominance conditions applied to KSL, and 'In Kuwaiti Sign Language, only seven handshapes are allowed for a stationary hand' (p. 16); the passive-hand handshapes are listed as h - n - sˁ - s - b - ʔ - 5 (p. 15). The only prosody-like remark is generic ('its use of movement to convey the rise and fall of the voice', p. 18), about sign languages in general.

sources.citation: Al-Fityani, Kinda & Carol Padden. 2010. Sign languages in the Arab world. In Diane Brentari (ed.), Sign Languages (Cambridge Language Surveys), 433-450. Cambridge: CUP. doi:10.1017/cbo9780511712203.020 [author preprint 'Sign Language Geography in the Arab World', 22 pp.]

sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical comparison of KSL with Jordanian, Libyan, Palestinian and Al-Sayyid Bedouin SL using the Kuwaiti Sign Language Dictionary (1995) (fn. 4, p. 10); signs compared on four phonemic parameters only.

sources.citation: Al-Fityani, Kinda. 2010. Deaf people, modernity, and a contentious effort to unify Arab sign languages. PhD dissertation, University of California, San Diego.
